arxiv-2002-03965.title: Palindromic k-Factorization in Pure Linear Time
arxiv-2002-03965.creator: Mikhail Rubinchik, Arseny M. Shur
arxiv-2002-03965.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Mikhail Rubinchik, Arseny M. Shur. Given a string s s of length n n over a general alphabet and an integer k k , the problem is to decide whether s s is a concatenation of k k nonempty palindromes. Two previously known solutions for this problem work in time O ⁡ ( k ​ n ) O(kn) and O ⁡ ( n ​ log ⁡ n ) O(n\log n) respectively.

arxiv-2111-02538.title: Exploring the AGN-ram pressure stripping connection in local clusters
arxiv-2111-02538.creator: Giorgia Peluso, Benedetta Vulcani, Bianca M. Poggianti, Alessia Moretti, Mario Radovich, Rory Smith, Yara L. Jaffé, Jacob Crossett, Marco Gullieuszik, Jacopo Fritz, Alessandro Ignesti
arxiv-2111-02538.description: Abstract Ram-pressure stripping by the intracluster medium (ICM) is one of the most advocated mechanisms that affect the properties of cluster galaxies. A recent study based on a small sample has found that many galaxies showing strong signatures of ram-pressure stripping also possess an active galactic nucleus (AGN), suggesting a possible correlation between the two phenomena.

arxiv-2112-03916.title: BT-Unet: A self-supervised learning framework for biomedical image segmentation using Barlow Twins with U-Net models
arxiv-2112-03916.creator: Narinder Singh Punn, Sonali Agarwal
arxiv-2112-03916.description: Abstract Deep learning has brought the most profound contribution towards biomedical image segmentation to automate the process of delineation in medical imaging. To accomplish such task, the models are required to be trained using huge amount of annotated or labelled data that highlights the region of interest with a binary mask.

arxiv-2308-16526.title: Gravity-induced entanglement between two massive microscopic particles in curved spacetime: I. The Schwarzschild background
arxiv-2308-16526.creator: Chi Zhang, Fu-Wen Shu
arxiv-2308-16526.description: Abstract The experiment involving the entanglement of two massive particles through gravitational fields has been devised to discern the quantum attributes of gravity. In this paper, we present a scheme to extend this experiment’s applicability to more generalized curved spacetimes, with the objective of validating universal quantum gravity within broader contexts.

arxiv-2310-10211.title: GEVO-ML: Optimizing Machine Learning Code with Evolutionary Computation DOI: 10.1145/nnnnnnn.nnnnnnn ISBN: 978-x-xxxx-xxxx-x/YY/MM Conference: The Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference 2021; July 10–14, 2021; Lille, France
arxiv-2310-10211.creator: Jhe-Yu Liou, Stephanie Forrest, Carole-Jean Wu
arxiv-2310-10211.description: Abstract . Parallel accelerators, such as GPUs, are key enablers for large-scale Machine Learning (ML) applications. However, ML model developers often lack detailed knowledge of the underlying system architectures, while system programmers usually do not have a high-level understanding of the ML model that runs on the specific system.

arxiv-2401-00707.title: A test of MOND and Emergent Gravity with SMACS J0723.3-7327 using eROSITA observations
arxiv-2401-00707.creator: Ambica Govind, Shantanu Desai
arxiv-2401-00707.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ambica Govind, Shantanu Desai. We implement a test of MOND and Verlinde’s Emergent Gravity using the galaxy cluster SMACS J0723-7327, which has been recently imaged using the eROSITA X-ray telescope as well as with JWST. We test MOND using two independent methods. The first method involves comparing the dynamical MOND mass and baryonic mass, while the second method entails a comparison of the MOND-estimated temperature with the observed temperature.

britannica-1911-quenstedt-friedrich-augu.title: Quenstedt, Friedrich August von (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-quenstedt-friedrich-augu.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-quenstedt-friedrich-augu.description: Article 'Quenstedt, Friedrich August von' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 22), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. German geologist and palaeontologist, was born at Eisleben in Saxony on the 9th of July 1809. He was educated at Berlin, and after having acted as assistant in the mineralogical museum he was appointed professor of mineralogy and geognosy in the university of Tübingen in 1837, a post which he occupied until his death.

britannica-1911-walmer.title: Walmer (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-walmer.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-walmer.description: Article 'Walmer' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 28), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. of Sandwich, in the St Augustine's parliamentary division of  Kent, England, 2 m. of Deal, on the South-Eastern & Chatham railway. of urban district (1901) 5248. Lower Walmer, the portion most frequented by visitors, extends northward along the coast, so as to be contiguous with Deal. Upper Walmer is a short distance uiland, and below it Walmer Castle lies close to the sea.

pmc-10652758.title: Modeling the crosstalk between malignant B cells and their microenvironment in B-cell lymphomas: challenges and opportunities
pmc-10652758.creator: Baptiste Brauge, Elise Dessauge, Florent Creusat, Karin Tarte
pmc-10652758.description: B-cell lymphomas are a group of heterogeneous neoplasms resulting from the clonal expansion of mature B cells arrested at various stages of differentiation. Specifically, two lymphoma subtypes arise from germinal centers (GCs), namely follicular lymphoma (FL) and GC B-cell diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (GCB-DLBCL).

pmc-10674088.title: Establishing a national research software award
pmc-10674088.creator: Isabelle Blanc Catala, Roberto Di Cosmo, Mathieu Giraud, Daniel Le Berre, Violaine Louvet, Sophie Renaudin, College of experts for source code and software Committee for Open Science, Jesús M. González Barahona, Karthik Ram
pmc-10674088.description: Software development has become an integral part of the scholarly ecosystem, spanning all fields and disciplines. To support the sharing and creation of knowledge in line with open science principles, and particularly to enable the reproducibility of research results, it is crucial to make the source code of research software available, allowing for modification, reuse, and distribution.

pmc-11000835.title: Takotsubo Syndrome: Is It Just a “Broken Heart”?
pmc-11000835.creator: Haris Muhammad, Angila Bag, Aparna Iyer
pmc-11000835.description: egional wall motion abnormalities seen on echocardiogram. Hence, TTS is also called “apical ballooning syndrome”. While the prevalence of TTS remains mixed across various studies, it is estimated that TTS accounts for 1%–3% of cases of acute coronary syndrome (ACS).2,3 TTS is classified as either primary or secondary based on patient presentation.

pmc-11402680.title: Causal relationship between modifiable risk factors and knee osteoarthritis: a Mendelian randomization study
pmc-11402680.creator: Zhihao Diao, Danyang Guo, Jingzhi Zhang, Ruiyu Zhang, Chunjing Li, Hao Chen, Yuxia Ma
pmc-11402680.description: BackgroundWhile several risk factors for knee osteoarthritis (KOA) have been recognized, the pathogenesis of KOA and the causal relationship between modifiable risk factors and KOA in genetic epidemiology remain unclear. This study aimed to determine the causal relationship between KOA and its risk factors.MethodsData were obtained from published Genome-Wide Association study (GWAS) databases.

pmc-11437213.title: Structural basis of ligand recognition and activation of the histamine receptor family
pmc-11437213.creator: Xuan Zhang, Guibing Liu, Ya-Ni Zhong, Ru Zhang, Chuan-Cheng Yang, Canyang Niu, Xuanyu Pu, Jingjing Sun, Tianyao Zhang, Lejin Yang, Chao Zhang, Xiu Li, Xinyuan Shen, Peng Xiao, Jin-Peng Sun, Weimin Gong
pmc-11437213.description: Histamine is a biogenic amine that is critical in various physiological and pathophysiological processes, including but not limited to allergic reactions, wakefulness, gastric acid secretion and neurotransmission. Here, we determine 9 cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of the 4 histamine receptors in complex with four different G protein subtypes, with endogenous or synthetic agonists bound.

pmc-11464697.title: New tunneling source follower with low 1/f noise and high voltage gain
pmc-11464697.creator: Ki Yeong Kim, Hyangwoo Kim, Minkeun Choi, Kyounghwan Oh, Hyeongseok Yoo, Yijoon Kim, Yoon Sol, Sungbong Park, Jae-Kyu Lee, Chang-Ki Baek
pmc-11464697.description: We have designed a tunneling source follower (TSF) for image sensors that achieves high voltage gain (Av) and low 1/f noise simultaneously. The TSF is composed of N-P-N-N, especially the p-doped grounded area, which serves to amplify the insufficient tunneling current, allowing the source follower (SF) to utilize band-to-band tunneling (BTBT).

pmc-11477279.title: Differential Fatty Acid Response of Resident Macrophages in Human Skeletal Muscle Fiber and Intermuscular Adipose Tissue
pmc-11477279.creator: Xiaoying Chen, Aline Müller, Miguel Pishnamaz, Frank Hildebrand, Leo Cornelius Bollheimer, Mahtab Nourbakhsh, Waipo Chong, Daniela Novick
pmc-11477279.description: Human skeletal muscle contains different types of tissues with skeletal muscle fibers (SMFs) and intermuscular adipose tissues (IMATs) as the main components. We maintained human skeletal muscle tissues from 12 study participants under native conditions in vitro for 11 days to investigate the dynamics of macrophages that reside in adjacent IMATs and SMFs simultaneously.

pmc-11640129.title: Hybrid Deep Learning and Machine Learning for Detecting Hepatocyte Ballooning in Liver Ultrasound Images
pmc-11640129.creator: Fahad Alshagathrh, Mahmood Alzubaidi, Samuel Gecík, Khalid Alswat, Ali Aldhebaib, Bushra Alahmadi, Meteb Alkubeyyer, Abdulaziz Alosaimi, Amani Alsadoon, Maram Alkhamash, Jens Schneider, Mowafa Househ
pmc-11640129.description: Background: Hepatocyte ballooning (HB) is a significant histological characteristic linked to the advancement of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). Although clinicians now consider liver biopsy the most reliable method for identifying HB, its invasive nature and related dangers highlight the need for the development of non-invasive diagnostic options.

pmc-11646295.title: The emerging role of Fusobacteria in carcinogenesis
pmc-11646295.creator: Raisha J. Gibbs, Adam C. Chambers, Darryl J. Hill
pmc-11646295.description: The Fusobacterium genus comprises Gram‐negative, obligate anaerobic bacteria that typically reside in the periodontium of the oral cavity, gastrointestinal tract, and female genital tract. The association of Fusobacterial spp. with colorectal tumours is widely accepted, with further evidence that this pathogen may also be implicated in the development of other malignancies. pmc-11732538.title: Advances in lysosomal escape mechanisms for gynecological cancer nano-therapeutics
pmc-11732538.creator: Heng Wei, Yingying Hao, Jin Zhang, Yue Qi, Chong Feng, Chen Zhang
pmc-11732538.description: Gynecological cancers present significant treatment challenges due to drug resistance and adverse side effects. This review explores advancements in lysosomal escape mechanisms, essential for enhancing nano-therapeutic efficacy. Strategies such as pH-sensitive linkers and membrane fusion are examined, showcasing their potential to improve therapeutic outcomes in ovarian, cervical, and uterine cancers.

pmc-11736655.title: Dietary fat quality indices and risk of pre-diabetes and type 2 diabetes mellitus: Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study
pmc-11736655.creator: Zahra Gaeini, Sevda Alvirdizadeh, Somayeh Hosseinpour-Niazi, Parvin Mirmiran, Fereidoun Azizi
pmc-11736655.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Objective:To assess associations between dietary fat quality indices and risk of pre-diabetes and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) among Iranian adults.Design:Daily intakes of fatty acids were estimated using a validated FFQ with 168 food items.

pmc-12563115.title: Mechanisms Underlying the Changes in the Digestive Properties of Chicken Breasts Induced by the Changes in Protein Structure During Frozen Storage
pmc-12563115.creator: Xue Bai, Quanyu Zhang, Tingting Zhang, Ying Yu, Xin Du, Xiufang Xia
pmc-12563115.description: This study aimed to investigate the effects of different freezing temperatures and storage durations on the digestive and structural properties of chicken meat proteins. The texture, protein digestibility, particle size, and microstructure of the digested samples were used to characterize their digestive properties.

pmc-12612932.title: Placental Vascular Resistance and Offspring Growth From Birth to Age 2 Years
pmc-12612932.creator: Luli Xu, Jin’e Zhang, Kai Chen, Xiaohan Dong, Xiya Qin, Mingzhao Huang, DeMing Kong, Xiaoxuan Fan, Xiaofeng Mu, Lianting Hu, Yuji Wang, Zhiguo Xia, Jun Li, Aifen Zhou, Chao Xiong
pmc-12612932.description: Key PointsQuestionWhat is the association of placental vascular resistance with children’s physical growth after birth?FindingsThis cohort study in 52 660 mother-infant pairs found that elevated placental vascular resistance was associated with higher risks of underweight and impaired growth during early childhood.

pmc-12798876.title: Effect of Vibration, Electrical Stimulation and Other Non-Pharmacological Interventions on Restless Leg Syndrome Severity and Sleep Quality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-12798876.creator: Bhupesh Gupta, Ramita Goel, Kirtika Gupta, Arpitkumar Thakor, Anshu Mittal
pmc-12798876.description: Background and Objectives:This study aims to determine the effect of nonpharmacological treatments, such as vibration, electric stimulation, acupressure, massage therapy, cryotherapy, and exercise, on the restless legs syndrome (RLS) severity score.Methods:Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines were followed for selecting studies to be included in the meta-analysis.

pmc-13064228.title: Patient perspectives on practice guidance in nursing education: a scoping review
pmc-13064228.creator: Andrea Glodek, Bettina Dauer, Bernd Reuschenbach
pmc-13064228.description: BackgroundPractical training in health care involves caring for patients in hospitals, long-term care facilities, and outpatient settings. This scoping review examines patients’ perspectives on their involvement in clinical teaching and explores how evidence from medical education can guide nursing education when research is lacking.MethodsA systematic search of PubMed, CINAHL, and LIVIVO was conducted.

pmc-13101536.title: Coexistence process and driving factors of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi in urban green soil under heavy metal stress
pmc-13101536.creator: Haopu Li, Yazhou Feng, Zhonghu Geng, Mengyao Zhang, Yiming Cui, Yizhen Shao, Yun Chen, Zhiliang Yuan
pmc-13101536.description: Urban green spaces in rapidly developing cities face severe heavy metal (HM) pollution, yet how this pollution affects arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal (AMF) community assembly remains poorly understood. This study involved the collection of 60 soil samples from green spaces throughout Zhengzhou, China. Soil edaphic factors and levels of five HMs were measured, alongside the sequencing of AMF communities.

pmc-13533634.title: Age‐Related and Seasonal Variation in Malaria and Other Causes of Fever and Their Association With Clinical Outcomes in Southern Angola: A Hospital‐Based Study
pmc-13533634.creator: Helga E. M. Gonçalves, Maria Lina Antunes, Jorge Seixas, Marcelo U. Ferreira
pmc-13533634.description: BackgroundAcute febrile illnesses in sub‐Saharan Africa are often attributed to malaria, yet many patients test negative for malaria parasites. The aetiology of nonmalarial fevers remains understudied. Here, we examine likely causes of febrile illnesses and their association with poor clinical outcomes in Angola.

pmc-13598134.title: Modeling Friedreich’s ataxia with Bergmann glia-enriched human cerebellar organoids
pmc-13598134.creator: Seungmi Ryu, Jason Inman, Hyenjong Hong, Vukasin M Jovanovic, Qiang Chen, Yeliz Gedik, Yogita Jethmalani, Inae Hur, Majid Harouni, Ty Voss, Justin Lack, Jack Collins, Pinar Ormanoglu, Anton Simeonov, Carlos A Tristan, Ilyas Singeç
pmc-13598134.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The human cerebellum is implicated in various neurological and psychiatric diseases, but its complex development and cellular diversity have posed challenges for in vitro modeling. Here, we report the generation of human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cerebellar organoids (hCBOs) that are characterized by induction of rhombomere 1 (R1) cellular identity and followed by derivation of typical neuronal and glial cell types of the cerebellum.
